title: Technology Sector Update for 07/17/2018: MDSO,IQ,ADSK - Nasdaq.com
text:

Technology stocks were mostly higher Tuesday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 rising over 0.6% while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has jumped out to a more than 0.8% increase.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Medidata Solutions ( MDSO ) was nearly 5% higher early Tuesday afternoon, stretching out its advance throughout the session after analysts at RBC Capital Markets raised their investment rating for the cloud-based analytics platform for life sciences companies to Outperform from Sector Perform and also increased its price target for the company's stock by $17 to $100 a share. In a note to clients, RBC said Medidata Solutions was "well-positioned to capitalize on a favorable drug-research funding environment, as well as capital inflows as health care investors look to stocks not afflicted by an Amazon overhang and the precarious generic-drug pricing environment."
In other sector news:
+ iQIYI ( IQ ) was almost 1% higher Tuesday afternoon, erasing an more than 5% decline earlier in the session, after the Chinese online entertainment said it has completed its buyout of Skymoons and Chengdu Skymoons Digital Entertainment. iQIYI paid RMB1.27 billion, or about $189.8 million, for the mobile games developer as well as a conditional RMB730 million payment as Skymoons reaches certain performance milestones over the next two years. In addition to mobile games, Skymoons also has existing deals for the development and promotion of films, anime and comics.
- Autodesk ( ADSK ) has pared a portion of its more than 1% decline Tuesday afternoon that followed the software company late Monday disclosing plans to register 340,769 shares of its common stock issued to a dozen shareholders affiliated with Autodesk's July 3 acquisition of Assemble Systems. The shareholders include a handful of institutional investors - Built Environmental Innovation Fund, Redhouse Associates and Satterfield Investments - along with other Assemble Systems insiders. The shares being registered include shares held by Computershare in escrow to fund potential indemnification obligations, and once registered, can be sold by the shareholders at their discretion.
